Founded in 1899 by a group of Swiss, Catalan, German, and English footballers led by [Joan Gamper](/wiki/Joan_Gamper "Joan Gamper"), the club has become a symbol of Catalan culture and [Catalanism](/wiki/Catalanism "Catalanism"), hence the motto *Més que un club* ("More than a club").[[1]](#cite_note-1) Unlike many other football clubs, [the supporters](/wiki/Supporters_of_FC_Barcelona "Supporters of FC Barcelona") own and operate Barcelona. It is the third-most valuable football club in the world, worth $5.6 billion, and the [world's fourth richest](/wiki/Deloitte_Football_Money_League "Deloitte Football Money League") football club in terms of revenue, with an annual turnover of €800.1 million.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) The official Barcelona anthem is the "[Cant del Barça](/wiki/Cant_del_Bar%C3%A7a "Cant del Barça")", written by [Jaume Picas i Guiu](/w/index.php?title=Jaume_Picas_i_Guiu&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jaume Picas i Guiu (page does not exist)") and [Josep Maria Espinàs](/wiki/Josep_Maria_Espin%C3%A0s "Josep Maria Espinàs").[[4]](#cite_note-4) Barcelona traditionally play in dark shades of blue and [garnet](/wiki/Shades_of_red#Garnet "Shades of red") stripes, hence nicknamed *Blaugrana*.

Barcelona are one of the [world's most decorated clubs](/wiki/List_of_football_clubs_by_competitive_honours_won "List of football clubs by competitive honours won"). Domestically, Barcelona has won a record 81 trophies: 28 [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), 32 [Copa del Rey](/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey"), 2 [Copa de la Liga](/wiki/Copa_de_la_Liga "Copa de la Liga"), 16 [Supercopa de España](/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España") and 3 [Copa Eva Duarte](/wiki/Copa_Eva_Duarte "Copa Eva Duarte") titles, as well as being the record holder for the latter four competitions. In [international club football](/wiki/FC_Barcelona_in_international_football "FC Barcelona in international football"), Barça has won 22 European and worldwide titles: five [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") titles, a record four [UEFA Cup Winners' Cups](/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup "UEFA Cup

Beagle :: History :: Development of the modern breed :: chunk_0002
Reverend Phillip Honeywood established a Beagle pack in [Essex](/wiki/Essex "Essex") in the 1830s; it is believed that this pack formed the basis for the modern breed. Although details of the pack's lineage are not recorded, it is thought that North Country Beagles and Southern Hounds were strongly represented; [William Youatt](/wiki/William_Youatt "William Youatt") suspected that [Harriers](/wiki/Harrier_(dog) "Harrier (dog)") formed a good majority of the Beagle's bloodline, but the origin of the Harrier is itself obscure.[[1]](#cite_note-Y110-1) Honeywood's Beagles were small, standing at about 10 inches (25 cm) at the shoulder, and pure white according to John Mills (writing in *The Sportsman's Library* in 1845). [Prince Albert](/wiki/Albert,_Prince_Consort "Albert, Prince Consort") and [Lord Winterton](/wiki/Edward_Turnour,_4th_Earl_Winterton "Edward Turnour, 4th Earl Winterton") also had Beagle packs around this time, and royal favour no doubt led to some revival of interest in the breed, but Honeywood's pack was regarded as the finest of the three.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/4-beagles.jpg/250px-4-beagles.jpg)](/wiki/File:4-beagles.jpg)

Early images of the Beagle (clockwise from top left): 1833, 1835, [Stonehenge](/wiki/John_Henry_Walsh "John Henry Walsh")'s Medium (1859, reusing [Youatt](/wiki/William_Youatt "William Youatt")'s 1852 "Beagle" image) and Dwarf Beagle (1859).

Although credited with the development of the modern breed, Honeywood concentrated on producing dogs for hunting and it was left to Thomas Johnson to refine the breeding to produce dogs that were both attractive and capable hunters. Two strains were developed: the rough-coated and smooth-coated varieties. The rough-coated beagle survived until the beginning of the 20th century, and there were even records of one making an appearance at a dog show as late as 1969, but this variety is now extinct, having probably been absorbed into the standard beagle bloodline.[[8]](#cite_note-K7-8)

Arabian Desert :: Geography :: chunk_0001
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Arabian_Desert.png/250px-Arabian_Desert.png)](/wiki/File:Arabian_Desert.png)

A satellite image of the Arabian Desert by [NASA World Wind](/wiki/NASA_World_Wind "NASA World Wind")

The desert lies mostly in [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") and covers most of the country. It extends into neighboring southern [Iraq](/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"), southern [Jordan](/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"), central [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), most of the [Abu Dhabi](/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") emirate in the [United Arab Emirates](/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), western [Oman](/wiki/Oman "Oman"), and northeastern [Yemen](/wiki/Yemen "Yemen"). The ecoregion also includes most of the [Sinai Peninsula](/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") in [Egypt](/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") and the adjacent [Negev](/wiki/Negev "Negev") desert in southern Israel.[[1]](#cite_note-dopa-1)

The [Rub' al-Khali](/wiki/Rub%27_al-Khali "Rub' al-Khali") desert is a [sedimentary basin](/wiki/Sedimentary_basin "Sedimentary basin") stretching along a south-west to north-east axis across the Arabian Shelf.[[5]](#cite_note-5) At an altitude of 1,000 metres (3,300 ft), rock landscapes yield to the Rub' al-Khali, a vast stretch of sand whose extreme southern point crosses the center of Yemen. The sand overlies gravel or gypsum plains and the dunes reach maximum heights of up to 250 m (820 ft). The sands are predominantly silicates, composed of 80 to 90% quartz and the remainder feldspar, whose iron oxide-coated grains color the sands orange, purple, and red.

A corridor of sandy terrain known as the [Ad-Dahna desert](/wiki/Ad-Dahna_desert "Ad-Dahna desert") connects the [An-Nafud desert](/wiki/Nefud "Nefud") (65,000 km2 or 40,389 square miles) in the north of Saudi Arabia to the Rub' al-Khali in the south-east. The [Tuwaiq](/wiki/Tuwaiq "Tuwaiq") escarpment is an 800 km (500 mi) arc that includes limestone cliffs, plateaus, and canyons. There are brackish salt flats, including the [quicksands](/wiki/Quicksand "Quicksand") of [Umm al Samim](/wiki/Umm_al_Samim "Umm al Samim").[[2]](#cite_note-ww

**Novak Djokovic**[[a]](#cite_note-7) (born 22 May 1987) is a Serbian professional [tennis](/wiki/Tennis "Tennis") player. Djokovic has been ranked as the [world No. 1](/wiki/List_of_ATP_number_1_ranked_singles_tennis_players#Weeks_at_No._1 "List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players") in men's singles by the [Association of Tennis Professionals](/wiki/Association_of_Tennis_Professionals "Association of Tennis Professionals") (ATP) for a record 428 weeks, finished as the [year-end No. 1](/wiki/List_of_ATP_number_1_ranked_singles_tennis_players#Year-end_No._1_players "List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players") a record eight times, and has been ranked No. 1 at least once in a year for a record 13 different years. He has won 101 [ATP Tour](/wiki/ATP_Tour "ATP Tour")–level singles titles, including a record 24 [majors](/wiki/List_of_Grand_Slam_men%27s_singles_champions "List of Grand Slam men's singles champions") (including a record ten [Australian Open](/wiki/Australian_Open "Australian Open") titles), a record 40 [Masters](/wiki/Tennis_Masters_Series_records_and_statistics#Title_leaders "Tennis Masters Series records and statistics"), a record seven [year-end championships](/wiki/ATP_Finals "ATP Finals"), and an [Olympic gold medal](/wiki/Tennis_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Tennis at the Summer Olympics"). Djokovic is the only man in tennis history to be the reigning champion of all four majors at once across three different surfaces. In singles, he is the only man to achieve a [triple Career Grand Slam](/wiki/List_of_Grand_Slam_men%27s_singles_champions#Career_Grand_Slam "List of Grand Slam men's singles champions"), and the only player to complete a [Career Golden Masters](/wiki/Tennis_Masters_Series_records_and_statistics#Career_Golden_Masters "Tennis Masters Series records and statistics"), a feat he has accomplished twice. Djokovic is the only player in singles to have won [all of the Big Titles](/wiki/List_of_ATP_Big_Titles_singles_champions#Big_Titles_sweep "List of ATP Big Titles singles champions") over the course of his career.

[State Route 33](/wiki/California_State_Route_33 "California State Route 33"), the Ojai Freeway, heads north to [Ojai](/wiki/Ojai,_California "Ojai, California"). [State Route 126](/wiki/California_State_Route_126 "California State Route 126") and [State Route 118](/wiki/California_State_Route_118 "California State Route 118") head east to [Santa Clarita](/wiki/Santa_Clarita,_California "Santa Clarita, California") and [Simi Valley](/wiki/Simi_Valley,_California "Simi Valley, California"), respectively.

[Ventura–East station](/wiki/Ventura%E2%80%93East_station "Ventura–East station"), in the historic [Montalvo](/wiki/Montalvo,_Ventura,_California "Montalvo, Ventura, California") neighborhood, serves as the western terminus of the [Ventura County Line](/wiki/Ventura_County_Line "Ventura County Line") of the [Metrolink](/wiki/Metrolink_(California) "Metrolink (California)") commuter rail system, which extends to [Union Station in Los Angeles](/wiki/Union_Station_(Los_Angeles) "Union Station (Los Angeles)"). The downtown [Ventura Amtrak Station](/wiki/Ventura_station "Ventura station") is served by Amtrak's *[Pacific Surfliner](/wiki/Pacific_Surfliner "Pacific Surfliner")* from [San Luis Obispo](/wiki/San_Luis_Obispo,_California "San Luis Obispo, California") to [San Diego](/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego").

Manchester United has been described as a global brand; a 2011 report by Brand Finance, valued the club's trademarks and associated intellectual property at £412 million – an increase of £39 million on the previous year, valuing it at £11 million more than the second best brand, Real Madrid – and gave the brand a strength rating of AAA (Extremely Strong).[[176]](#cite_note-178) In July 2012, Manchester United was ranked first by *[Forbes](/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* magazine in its list of the ten most valuable sports team brands, valuing the Manchester United brand at $2.23 billion.[[177]](#cite_note-179) The club is ranked third in the [Deloitte Football Money League](/wiki/Deloitte_Football_Money_League "Deloitte Football Money League") (behind Real Madrid and Barcelona).[[178]](#cite_note-Deloitte_money_league-180) In January 2013, the club became the first sports team in the world to be valued at $3 billion.[[179]](#cite_note-bstonfrbs-181) *Forbes* magazine valued the club at $3.3 billion – $1.2 billion higher than the next most valuable sports team.[[179]](#cite_note-bstonfrbs-181) They were overtaken by Real Madrid for the next four years, but Manchester United returned to the top of the *Forbes* list in June 2017, with a valuation of $3.689 billion.[[180]](#cite_note-182)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg/250px-Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg)](/wiki/File:Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg)

[Edmund Hillary](/wiki/Edmund_Hillary "Edmund Hillary") and [Tenzing Norgay](/wiki/Tenzing_Norgay "Tenzing Norgay")

In 1953, a ninth British expedition, led by [John Hunt](/wiki/John_Hunt,_Baron_Hunt "John Hunt, Baron Hunt"), returned to Nepal. Hunt selected two climbing pairs to attempt the summit. The first, [Tom Bourdillon](/wiki/Tom_Bourdillon "Tom Bourdillon") and [Charles Evans](/wiki/Charles_Evans_(mountaineer) "Charles Evans (mountaineer)"), came within 100 m (330 ft) of the summit on 26 May 1953, but turned back after running into oxygen problems. As planned, their work in routefinding, breaking trail and oxygen caches were of great aid to the following pair. Two days later, the expedition made its second assault with the second pair: New Zealander [Edmund Hillary](/wiki/Edmund_Hillary "Edmund Hillary") and [Tenzing Norgay](/wiki/Tenzing_Norgay "Tenzing Norgay"), a Nepali [Sherpa](/wiki/Sherpa_people "Sherpa people") climber. They reached the summit at 11:30 am local time on 29 May 1953 via the South Col route. At the time, both acknowledged it as a team effort by the whole expedition, but Tenzing revealed a few years later that Hillary had put his foot on the summit first.[[114]](#cite_note-Ullman-122) They took photos and buried sweets and a small cross in the snow before descending.[[115]](#cite_note-123)

On [Spotify](/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), Bad Bunny has been named the platform's most-streamed artist globally a record four times (2020, 2021, 2022, and 2025), making him the first and only artist to achieve this distinction.[[235]](#cite_note-237) In 2020, he became the first non-English language artist to top Spotify's year-end most-streamed list.[[236]](#cite_note-238) His 2025 total of 19.8 billion streams was driven largely by *Debí Tirar Más Fotos*, which was also named the most-streamed album globally that year.[[237]](#cite_note-239)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Ryan_Fitzpatrick_2016.jpg/250px-Ryan_Fitzpatrick_2016.jpg)](/wiki/File:Ryan_Fitzpatrick_2016.jpg)

Fitzpatrick with the Jets in 2016

Fitzpatrick, a free agent after the 2015 season, signed a one-year fully guaranteed $12 million contract with the Jets on July 27, 2016.[[89]](#cite_note-89)

During the narrow season-opening 23–22 loss to the [Cincinnati Bengals](/wiki/2016_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2016 Cincinnati Bengals season"), Fitzpatrick threw for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.[[90]](#cite_note-90) In the next game on *Thursday Night Football* against the [Buffalo Bills](/wiki/2016_Buffalo_Bills_season "2016 Buffalo Bills season"), he gradually improved with 374 passing yards and a touchdown, leading the Jets to a 37–31 victory to earn AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[91]](#cite_note-91)[[92]](#cite_note-92) The following week against the [Kansas City Chiefs](/wiki/2016_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2016 Kansas City Chiefs season"), the Jets committed eight turnovers, including Fitzpatrick throwing six interceptions. Fitzpatrick finished with 188 passing yards as the Jets lost on the road by a score of 24–3.[[93]](#cite_note-93) During a Week 6 28–3 road loss to the [Arizona Cardinals](/wiki/2016_Arizona_Cardinals_season "2016 Arizona Cardinals season"), Fitzpatrick was benched for Geno Smith after going 16-for-31 for 174 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception.[[94]](#cite_note-94)
